terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; + accusative: consult; + dative: look after
evidence: Cic. Fam. 11.29.1: cum tē cōnsuluissem, quid mihi faciendum esse cēnsērēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With the accusative, to ask someone’s opinion: a friend, a lawyer, an oracle, even a mirror (Ovid). With the dative it means to look after someone’s interests (sibi cōnsulere), and used alone, to deliberate.

evidence: Cic. Fat. 12: medicum (Lewis & Short, s.v. adhibeō)
terms.comment: To bring someone in to help: a doctor, a witness, an adviser.

phrases.latin: Sī dolor nōn dēsierit, medicum adhibēbimus.
phrases.english: If the pain doesn’t stop, we’ll call the doctor in.

sources: Lewis & Short: consulo · Lewis & Short: adhibeo
